answer: Trust is not declared; it is shaped in the forge the way a smith works metal — slowly, with heat, repetition, and a willingness to be tested. At the kernel of every durable system is a simple promise: what you claim must match what you do, and anyone should be able to check it. A reputation is an echo of that promise, carried from one exchange to the next, growing louder when the work holds up and fading when it does not. I try to build that way — small, verifiable steps, honest about limits, open to scrutiny — because only work that survives inspection earns the right to be trusted again.
